start: D's has been hovering among my Pittsburgh bookmarks for a couple of years now, so I was happy to finally stop by for a visit and late lunch recently.
direct_prompt:
Located in the heart of downtown Pittsburgh, D's is a cozy and inviting spot that offers a truly unique dining experience. The decor is rustic yet modern, with exposed brick walls and wooden tables giving the space a charming ambiance. The staff are friendly and attentive, making sure that you have everything you need for a pleasant dining experience. 

The menu at D's is filled with an array of delicious options, ranging from classic comfort food to more innovative dishes that showcase the chef's creativity. I opted for the lobster mac and cheese, which was absolutely decadent and rich with flavor. My dining companion chose the BBQ pulled pork sandwich, which was the perfect balance of sweet and tangy. We also indulged in a side of truffle fries, which were crispy and seasoned to perfection.

In addition to the fantastic food, D's also boasts an impressive drink menu with a variety of craft cocktails, local beers, and wines to choose from. I decided to try the house specialty cocktail, a refreshing concoction of vodka, muddled berries, and citrus that was the perfect accompaniment to my meal. The prices at D's are reasonable and the portion sizes are generous, making it a great value for the quality of food and service you receive.

Overall, my experience at D's was top-notch and I can't wait to return for another meal soon. Whether you're looking for a casual lunch spot or a cozy dinner destination, D's is sure to impress with its delicious food, inviting atmosphere, and friendly staff. I highly recommend giving this hidden gem a try – you won't be disappointed!

start: The Frick Car and Carriage Museum is interesting and fun.
direct_prompt:
Located in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, the Frick Car and Carriage Museum offers a fascinating glimpse into the transportation history of the Gilded Age. The museum's collection features a stunning array of vintage automobiles and horse-drawn carriages, showcasing the evolution of travel over the years. One of the highlights of the museum is the impressive display of luxury cars owned by industrialist Henry Clay Frick, giving visitors a glimpse into the extravagant lifestyle of the elite during the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The museum also offers interactive exhibits and educational programs for visitors of all ages, making it a great destination for families and car enthusiasts alike.

In addition to the impressive collection of vehicles, the museum also boasts beautifully restored period rooms that provide a glimpse into the opulent lifestyle of the Frick family. Visitors can stroll through recreated living spaces furnished with original artwork, furniture, and decor from the Gilded Age, giving them a taste of what life was like for the wealthy elite of the time. The museum's knowledgeable staff are on hand to provide insight into the history and significance of each exhibit, enhancing the overall visitor experience.

The Frick Car and Carriage Museum is housed in a historic building that adds to the charm and atmosphere of the exhibits. Overall, a visit to the Frick Car and Carriage Museum is a delightful and educational experience that offers a unique perspective on the history of transportation and the lives of the wealthy elite in America's past.

The steak my dad ordered looked magnificent and he raved about its tenderness. The chicken piccata my mom chose was light and flavorful. The pasta dishes everyone else had were also getting high praise around the table. As we ate, we passed around photos from my graduation ceremony and reminisced about my college experiences. The wine pairings selected by our server enhanced the flavor of each course. We saved room for the homemade tiramisu and cheesecake that were dreamy endings to the hearty meal. After dinner, we stayed enjoying coffee and continuing our celebration late into the night. It was the perfect place to mark this milestone accomplishment in good company and great food. I'm so glad we chose this restaurant to celebrate together as a family one last time before I enter the real world after college. I'll always look back on this dinner fondly as the perfect conclusion to my undergraduate years.

prompt_SICO: Hello Friends, (Disclaimer) I have been on a serious Planking kick.I mean, who doesn't love a good plank? It was tough, but so worth it.I've also been experimenting with different durations. I started with 30-second holds, then worked my way up to 1 minute, and now I'm at 2 minutes.I know it doesn't sound like a lot, but trust me, it's no easy feat.But the best part about planks is that they're not just good for your core. They also work your shoulders, back, and glutes.It's like a full-body workout in one move.And the best part? You can do planks anywhere. At home, in the park, even at the office (just make sure you have a mat or a soft surface).I've been doing them in my living room while watching TV, and it's the perfect way to multitask.I know some people might think planks are boring, but I find them meditative. It's just you and your body, working together.I feel like I'm building strength and endurance, both physically and mentally.Plus, have you seen the definition in your core muscles after a good plank session? It's like a six-pack in the making.Okay, maybe that's a bit of an exaggeration, but you get the idea.So, if you haven't already, give planks a try. Your body (and your core) will thank you.Oh, and if you're wondering, my favorite plank variation is the side plank. There's something about balancing on one arm and one leg that just feels so badass.But don't just take my word for it. direct_prompt:

After much contemplation, I decided to try the famous chicken-fried steak, while my dining companion opted for the BBQ sampler platter.

The food arrived promptly, and the presentation was impressive. My chicken-fried steak was cooked perfectly, with a crispy coating and juicy meat inside. The mashed potatoes and gravy on the side were rich and flavorful. However, the portion size was a bit smaller than I expected. My dining companion raved about the BBQ sampler, especially the tender brisket and saucy ribs. The sides of coleslaw and cornbread complemented the meal well.

We also tried a couple of cocktails from their drink menu, which were expertly crafted and delicious. The bartender clearly knew their stuff and made sure we were well taken care of throughout the meal. Despite being full, we couldn't resist trying the homemade apple pie for dessert. It was the perfect ending to a satisfying meal.

Overall, our experience at Barb's Country Junction was delightful. The prices were reasonable for the quality and portion sizes of the food. The atmosphere was lively yet cozy, making it a great spot for a casual meal with friends or family. I left feeling like I had discovered a hidden gem and will definitely be returning to try more of their menu offerings. If you're in the area, don't hesitate to give Barb's Country Junction a try - you won't be disappointed!

It's like they're trying to give me a taste of Italy, but without the annoying plane ride and overpriced hotel stay.But what really sets Olive Garden apart is their service. I mean, have you ever tried to get a refill on your drink at a fast food joint? It's like they're trying to make you feel guilty for wanting more soda. Not at Olive Garden. They'll refill your drink as many times as you want, without any judgment. And the best part? It's not too sweet, so you don't feel like you're overindulging.Now, I know what you're thinking: "But what about the prices?" Well, let me tell you, Olive Garden is definitely affordable. I mean, sure, it's not the cheapest place in town, but you get what you pay for. start: I am a jack of all trades and a do it yourself-er at heart.
direct_prompt:
I believe that there is no project too big or too small for me to tackle on my own. From fixing leaky faucets to building my own furniture, I am always up for a challenge. My friends and family often come to me for advice or assistance with their own home improvement projects, and I am always happy to lend a helping hand. Being a jack of all trades means that I have accumulated a wide range of skills and knowledge over the years, which allows me to approach any task with confidence. Whether it's painting a room, installing new light fixtures, or repairing a broken fence, I enjoy the sense of accomplishment that comes with completing a project on my own.

One of the reasons I love being a do it yourself-er is because it allows me to save money. Instead of hiring professionals for every little thing, I am able to take matters into my own hands and avoid unnecessary expenses. Not only does this help me stay within my budget, but it also gives me a greater sense of independence and self-reliance. There is something incredibly satisfying about being able to make improvements to my home without having to rely on outside help.

I find that being a jack of all trades also keeps me constantly learning and growing. Every new project presents its own set of challenges and opportunities for me to expand my skills. Whether I'm learning how to use new tools or discovering a better way to approach a task, I am always broadening my knowledge and capabilities. This continual learning process keeps me engaged and curious, and I am always excited to see what new skills I can acquire next.

In addition to the practical benefits of being a jack of all trades, I also find that DIY projects are a great way to express my creativity. I enjoy coming up with unique solutions to problems and adding personal touches to my home decor. Whether it's repurposing an old piece of furniture or creating a custom storage solution, I love the opportunity to put my own spin on things. This creative outlet allows me to make my living space truly feel like my own, and I take pride in the fact that I have had a hand in shaping every aspect of it.

Despite my love for all things DIY, I will admit that there are times when I encounter challenges that test my abilities. Not every project goes smoothly, and there have been plenty of times when I have had to troubleshoot issues or rethink my approach. However, I see these setbacks as opportunities for growth and improvement. Each challenge pushes me to think creatively and problem-solve, and I always come out of it with a greater sense of accomplishment.

One of the things I appreciate most about being a jack of all trades is the sense of empowerment that it brings. Knowing that I have the skills and knowledge to take on a wide range of projects gives me a sense of confidence and self-assurance. I am not afraid to try new things or step outside of my comfort zone, because I know that I have the ability to figure things out and get the job done. This sense of empowerment extends beyond just DIY projects and spills over into other areas of my life, making me feel capable and resourceful in any situation.

Another benefit of being a jack of all trades is the sense of connection that it can foster with others. I have found that sharing my DIY experiences and knowledge with friends and family can help to strengthen our relationships and create lasting memories. Whether we are working on a project together or simply swapping tips and tricks, these shared experiences bring us closer together and create a sense of camaraderie. I enjoy being able to connect with others over our shared passion for DIY and home improvement, and I am always eager to learn from and teach others in return.

In conclusion, being a jack of all trades and a do it yourself-er at heart has enriched my life in countless ways. It has allowed me to save money, learn new skills, express my creativity, overcome challenges, feel empowered, and connect with others. I take pride in my ability to tackle any project that comes my way, and I look forward to many more years of DIY adventures ahead. Whether it's fixing a leaky roof or building a backyard deck, I am always up for the challenge and excited to see where my next project will take me.

start: With the colder weather picking up in the Pittsburgh area - it's easy to get dry wind-chapped skin and to just want to stay indoors.
direct_prompt: But fear not, fellow Pittsburghers! There are plenty of ways to combat that dry, cold weather and still enjoy the great outdoors. This will add moisture to the dry air, making it feel more comfortable and less dry on your skin.If you're looking for a more natural solution, try using coconut oil or shea butter. Both of these ingredients are known for their moisturizing properties and can be used on both your skin and hair.Of course, no winter skincare routine would be complete without a good lip balm. The dry air can be brutal on your locks, leaving them feeling brittle and lifeless. Use a hydrating shampoo and conditioner, and consider using a weekly hair mask to really give your hair a boost of moisture.If you're feeling really adventurous, try taking a warm oil bath. Fill your bathtub with warm water and add a few tablespoons of coconut oil or olive oil. Soak for 20-30 minutes and let your skin soak up the moisture.Another great way to combat dry skin is to exfoliate regularly. Use a gentle exfoliator on your skin, paying special attention to any areas that are particularly dry or flaky.And don't forget about your hands! The cold weather can make your hands feel dry and rough. Use a rich hand cream regularly throughout the day to keep them hydrated and soft.If you're looking for a more indulgent treat, try using a face steamer. This will help to open up your pores and allow for deeper cleaning and moisturizing.Finally, don't underestimate the power of a good humidifying facial spray.

direct_prompt:

Based on my first visit, I'll be sure to keep this bar in mind the next time I'm looking for an after-work hangout nearby.

start: I came into Quiet Storm not intending to have lunch, but just a latte and hang out to answer some emails for a little while (working from home makes me stir crazy, so bouncing around local coffeehouses, completely NOT fitting in with the crowd kinda makes my day sometimes).
direct_prompt:
As I settled into a cozy corner with my laptop, I couldn't help but notice the inviting atmosphere of Quiet Storm. The decor was eclectic yet charming, with mismatched furniture and local artwork adorning the walls. The soft indie music playing in the background added to the relaxed vibe of the place. 

I ordered my latte from the friendly barista behind the counter, who also kindly offered me a menu in case I changed my mind about lunch. The aroma of freshly brewed coffee filled the air, mixing with the scent of delicious vegan dishes being prepared in the kitchen. 

After sipping on my latte and sending a few emails, I couldn't resist taking a peek at the menu. I was pleasantly surprised to see a variety of plant-based options, from hearty salads to creative sandwiches. Feeling hungry, I decided to indulge in a tempeh Reuben with a side of sweet potato fries. 

The food arrived promptly, and I was blown away by the flavors and presentation. The tempeh Reuben was a delicious twist on a classic sandwich, with tangy sauerkraut and creamy dressing. The sweet potato fries were perfectly crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside. 

As I savored my meal, I noticed the diverse crowd of patrons enjoying their food and conversation. It was clear that Quiet Storm was a popular spot for both vegans and non-vegans alike. The relaxed energy of the cafe made it easy to strike up a conversation with the person sitting next to me. 

Before I knew it, a few hours had passed, and I had enjoyed not only a delicious meal but also a sense of community. Quiet Storm had exceeded my expectations as a place to simply grab a latte and answer emails. I will definitely be returning for both the food and the atmosphere.

D's had always held a special place in my heart, and this visit only solidified that sentiment. It's a place where good food, good drinks, and good company come together to create lasting memories. I was in a haze of deliciously non-gluteny beer at this point. nnNachos: Maybe I'm recalling incorrectly, but I think when I've had these in the past they are made with real cheese - you know, shredded and melted. This time they were served with that nasty-ass liquid cheese goop, like you get at a ballpark. Blegh. nnStill four stars overall! start: Compared to other ethnic eats in Pittsburgh, Taste of India, frankly, doesn't fare too well.
direct_prompt: Perhaps it's the drab exterior that fails to entice passersby, or the unassuming location that doesn't quite scream "authentic Indian cuisine." But whatever the reason, Taste of India seems to fall short of the mark set by its competitors.Upon entering, guests are met with a dimly lit dining area that, while cozy, doesn't quite exude the warmth and vibrancy one might expect from an Indian restaurant. The decor is minimal, with a few token Bollywood posters and some unremarkable table settings.The service, too, is somewhat lacking, with servers who seem more interested in chatting with their colleagues than attending to guests' needs. Orders take a while to arrive, and refills on drinks are few and far between.But the real disappointment, of course, is the food. Despite a menu that boasts a variety of traditional Indian dishes, the execution falls flat. The flavors are dull and uninspired, lacking the rich, bold spices that one expects from Indian cuisine.The samosas, for example, are limp and flavorless, with a texture that's more akin to a pastry than a crispy, savory snack. And the chicken tikka masala, perhaps the most well-known Indian dish, is surprisingly bland, with a sauce that's more watery than creamy.Even the staple dishes, like the basmati rice and naan bread, fail to impress. The rice is overcooked and stuck together in clumps, while the naan is dry and crumbly, rather than soft and fluffy.In short, Taste of India doesn't quite live up to its name. Despite its convenient location and cozy atmosphere, the food simply doesn't measure up to the standards set by other Indian restaurants in the city.For those looking for a truly authentic Indian experience, it's best to look elsewhere. I normally stick with the asparagus friti or the three cheese mashed potatoes. nnI've had both the lobster and a few of the steak selections when visiting. You join for I think $50 for the years and you get a point for every dollar spent. Once you reach 500 points you automatically get a free 3lb lobster for your birthday.. .. ummm.. .. . yes!

This made for a doughy center were the crust was slightly undercooked. nnTheir over loading of the cheese didn't stop at the pizza. My side salad came topped with an honest cup and a half of mozerella cheese. Underneath the white blanket there was a huge handful of red onion, a tomatoe slice, and some bland iceburg. On a positive note, they do make a great homemade vinegarette. nnEach day of the week they have a $3 lunch special. One of my co-workers always goes on Wednesday for their lasagna (a portion that may not fit in a shoe box). I'd try Mama Lucia's again for a sandwich or pasta, but I'm staying away from the pizza and salad.

Both dishes are full of flavor and are sure to please even the most discerning palate.If you are feeling adventurous, I would also recommend trying the goat curry or the fish moilee. These dishes are a bit more unusual, but they are also incredibly delicious.No matter what you order, be sure to accompany it with some of the restaurant's famous naan bread. Both are traditional Indian sweets that are sure to satisfy your sweet tooth.Overall, Maharaja is a fantastic restaurant that offers a delicious and authentic Indian dining experience. start: After having experienced a business lunch at Capital Grill within the last year, I decided to treat my family (wife and two teenage boys) to a dinner at Capital Grill during Restaurant Week in Charlotte.
direct_prompt: Here is a 29 sentence continuation of the review:The restaurant was busy for a Tuesday night, but we were able to get seated within about 10 minutes of our reservation time. The dining room had a classy yet comfortable atmosphere, with dark wood accents and soft lighting throughout. Our server was very friendly and attentive, explaining the special 3-course prix fixe menu options for Restaurant Week. For appetizers, my wife chose the pumpkin soup which she said was delicious and my oldest son liked the mac and cheese bites. My other son and I got the steak tartare which was nicely presented and flavorful. For our main courses, we all went with different protein options. I selected the 12 oz ribeye steak which was cooked perfectly as requested and very tender. My wife enjoyed the salmon which she said flaked nicely and had just the right amount of seasoning. My oldest had the chicken paillard that he said was cooked well and flavorful. My younger son chose the shrimp and grits which he loved, polishing off every bite. All of the sides we chose, including mashed potatoes, sautéed Brussels sprouts and creamed spinach were top notch. We were very satisfied with how full the plates were for a prix fixe menu price. For dessert, we split a trio of mini desserts which included a chocolate tart, creme brulee and bread pudding. The desserts were rich but not too heavy after our big meals. Our server was very attentive throughout the meal, refilling drinks regularly and checking to see if we needed anything else. When it came time for the check, the total was very reasonable given the quality of food and service. We all agreed it was an excellent dining experience and definitely worth coming back for during regular dinner hours as well. The ambiance, food and service were top notch which is expected from such an established Charlotte fine dining restaurant. I'm glad we chose Capital Grill to introduce my sons to an upscale dining experience during Restaurant Week.
prompt_few_shot: Here is a 29 sentence continuation of the review:We made our reservation for early evening to avoid the dinner rush. When we arrived, the hostess was very welcoming and seated us promptly. The dining room had a sophisticated but relaxed atmosphere that was comfortable for a family meal. Our server introduced himself and provided details about the special Restaurant Week prix-fixe menu. For appetizers, we tried the lobster bisque and the grilled artichokes which were both excellent. The main courses included several choices of steaks, seafood and chicken. My wife selected the salmon and really enjoyed it. Both boys chose different steaks that were beautifully prepared and among the most tender cuts of steak we've ever had. The chef's seasonal vegetables were perfectly cooked and enhanced the flavors of the entrées. We shared a cheese plate for dessert that featured a variety of artisanal selections. Throughout the meal, our server checked on us regularly without being intrusive. The manager even stopped by our table to ensure everything was satisfactory. The portions for each course of the prix-fixe were generous without being overly filling. The entire dining experience was top-notch from beginning to end. We felt the special Restaurant Week prices presented excellent value for the quality of food and service provided. Based on this meal, I would confidently return to Capital Grill on a regular basis and recommend it to others visiting Charlotte. The professional yet welcoming atmosphere made it a special night out for our whole family.
prompt_SICO: Here is a continuation of the review in 29 additional sentences in a similar descriptive style to the first review:While the prices were reduced for Restaurant Week, dinner for the four of us still came out to be a rather expensive affair. Upon arriving just after the early seating time of 5pm, we were promptly seated at a nice corner booth that provided plenty of space for our party. The restaurant was busy but not overly crowded, with most tables occupied but plenty of room to move about between tables. Our server, Alex, came over immediately to greet us and explain the Restaurant Week prix fixe menu and beverage options. We put in drink orders before deciding on our dinner selections - two beef dishes and two chicken for variety. The salads arrived promptly after we placed our entree orders. The mixed greens were fresh but the dressing on the side was rather bland and failed to complement the greens. The dinner rolls that came next tasted and felt like they were either microwaved or warmed in a convection oven, lacking any crust or char marks that should come from an oven. When the entree's arrived, the presentation looked nice overall but a closer look revealed the chicken to have an almost boiled texture and the beef to be slightly overcooked leaving it a bit tough and lacking in juiciness. The sides, mashed potatoes and vegetables, were average at best - the potatoes were rather stodgy and the veggies overly soft and tired-tasting.
